children: The non-institutional investor (NII) category records the strongest demand, with subscription reaching 95.54 times the shares reserved for the segment
Shares of Shah Investor’s Home made a modest debut on the stock exchanges on Tuesday, listing at a 2.4 per cent premium to the issue price despite strong demand for the initial public offering (IPO).

The shares opened at Rs 171 apiece on both the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSE, compared with the IPO price of Rs 167. At the upper end of its price band, the company was valued at around Rs 353.25 crore.

The Rs 90.17-crore IPO, which was open for subscription between September 28 and September 30, received bids for around 14.27 crore shares against 37.39 lakh shares on offer, translating into an overall subscription of 38.12 times, according to NSE data.

The non-institutional investor (NII) category recorded the strongest demand, with subscription reaching 95.54 times the shares reserved for the segment. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) portion was subscribed 28.05 times, while the retail individual investor (RII) portion received 19.26 times subscription.
The company had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 159-167 per share.
Majority Of Proceeds For Working Capital
Shah Investor’s Home plans to deploy Rs 60 crore of the net IPO proceeds towards working capital requirements. The balance will be used for general corporate purposes.
The company operates in the financial services and securities market, with listed peers including SMC Global Securities, Share India Securities and Arihant Capital Markets.
Despite the strong investor response to its IPO, Shah Investor’s Home reported a decline in both revenue and profit in FY26.
Profit after tax fell 43.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 13.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 23.4 crore in the previous financial year. Revenue declined 24.2 per cent to Rs 71.5 crore from Rs 94.3 crore.
The company provides retail broking and related financial services. It has served more than 100,000 demat accounts and has over 38,000 active clients.
Shah Investor’s Home also has partnerships with more than 181 authorised persons and operates through 11 branches.
